did_you_know.text: Did you know? After the wall was completed, Nehemiah did not stop at installing the gates. He also appointed gatekeepers, singers, and Levites to organize the life of the city and the worship of God.
Did you know? Nehemiah placed his brother Hanani and Hananiah, the commander of the citadel, in charge of Jerusalem. He described Hananiah as a faithful man who feared God more than most people did.

Did you know? The gates of Jerusalem were not to be opened until the sun was hot, and they were to be closed and barred while the guards were still on duty. Guards were stationed near their own houses.
Did you know? Although Jerusalem was a large and spacious city, it had few inhabitants, and many houses had still not been built.
Did you know? Nehemiah gathered the nobles, officials, and people to register them by genealogy. Then he found a record containing the list of those who had first returned from exile.

Did you know? The list of those who returned begins with the leaders who came with Zerubbabel, including Jeshua and Nehemiah. After them, it lists the families of the people and the number of members in each family.

Did you know? After the families of the people, the list names the priestly families, followed by the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers—evidence of an organized division of responsibilities within the community.
Did you know? Chapter 7 also lists the families of the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants. Together, they belonged to groups who served within the community and the temple.

Did you know? Some of those who returned could not prove their family ancestry or their descent from Israel. Priesthood was withheld from families whose records could not be verified, and they were forbidden to eat the most holy food until the matter could be decided by a priest using the Urim and Thummim.
Did you know? The total number of people registered was 42,360, besides 7,337 male and female servants. The list also mentions 245 male and female singers, 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.
